bull.label: Escalation
bull.title: Scenario: Escalation
bull.description: Conflicts intensify or expand. More countries rearm. Defense spending keeps climbing. Pattern based on 2022–2023 escalation data.
bull.note: Based on 2022–2023 market behavior during active escalation phases. Defense stocks historically outperform strongly in this environment, but the human and fiscal costs also escalate. Note: high defense multiples today mean some upside may already be priced in.

base.label: Status Quo
base.title: Scenario: Status Quo
base.description: Current conflicts continue at similar intensity. Consistent with 2024–2025 SIPRI/NATO trajectory.
base.note: Status quo assumes current conflicts persist at roughly current intensity. Defense budgets continue growing at 4–6% annually. Commodity premiums stabilize at elevated levels. The most likely near-term path based on current trajectory.

bear.label: De-escalation
bear.title: Scenario: De-escalation
bear.description: Ukraine ceasefire. Diplomatic progress in Middle East. Defense stocks fall. Based on post-Cold War and post-Iraq 2003 drawdown patterns.
bear.note: Based on post-Cold War (1991) and post-Iraq (2003) drawdown patterns. Defense stocks would likely fall sharply — current valuations price in continued conflict. The reconstruction sector (infrastructure, housing) would see significant new demand.
